title_en: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
title_zh: 解析强到弱OPD与GRPO的计算效率对比
summary_en: This paper systematically compares on-policy distillation (OPD) with reverse-KL against Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) in terms of held-out accuracy per training FLOP across task difficulty, model sizes, domains, and optimization choices. With an external post-trained teacher, OPD generally underperforms GRPO at matched settings and often causes response-length inflation. However, when the teacher is the student's own GRPO checkpoint, OPD recovers that checkpoint's math accuracy with 50x fewer distillation FLOPs than GRPO requires. This efficiency holds for a larger student, on code, and in a second model family. Multi-teacher OPD consolidates per-domain GRPO experts into a single student matching each expert's accuracy, with distillation costing only 5.2% (2 domains) and 8.0% (more domains) of total compute.
summary_zh: 本文系统比较了基于反向KL的在线策略蒸馏（OPD）与组相对策略优化（GRPO）在任务难度、学生与教师规模、领域及优化选择等维度下，以训练FLOPs衡量的留出准确率。当教师为外部后训练模型时，OPD在同等设置下通常不如GRPO，且常出现回复长度膨胀。但当教师为学生自身的GRPO检查点时，OPD在数学任务上以比GRPO少50倍的蒸馏FLOPs恢复该检查点的准确率，该高效性在更大规模学生、代码任务及第二个模型家族中均成立。多教师OPD可将各领域GRPO专家整合为单一学生，匹配各专家准确率，蒸馏阶段仅占总计算量的5.2%（2个领域）和8.0%（更多领域）。
content_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher's per-token supervision. Does this dense signal reduce the training FLOPs needed to reach a target accuracy compared with reinforcement learning? We systematically compare vanilla reverse-KL OPD with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) across task difficulty, student and teacher size, domain, and optimization choices, measuring held-out accuracy against training FLOPs. With an external post-trained teacher, OPD generally loses to GRPO in accuracy per training FLOP at matched settings, even when the teacher is further trained with GRPO, and often suffers response-length inflation. Yet a different teacher changes the picture: when the teacher is the student's own GRPO checkpoint, OPD recovers that checkpoint's accuracy on math with $50\times$ fewer distillation FLOPs than GRPO needs to reach the same accuracy. Following the same teacher setting, we consistently observe this high efficiency with a larger student, on code, and in a second model family. On a single domain, however, the GRPO checkpoint is already the desired model, so distilling it adds to total compute. Across domains, separate GRPO checkpoints hold different capabilities, and no single checkpoint serves every domain.
